title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The Outline finally matches the code
summary: A class written the way ktlint wraps an injected constructor was read as one line long. Folding it folded nothing, and every one of its members hung outside it in the Outline and the breadcrumbs.

highlights.title: 202 misplaced nodes, now none
highlights.description: class Foo @Inject on one line and constructor(...) on the next is the shape Dagger imposes. The header was read as finished, so the class ended where it began.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A declaration whose header wraps after an annotation covers its whole body. On a real Android project 154 classes ended on their first line, so folding one folded nothing and its members were listed outside it.

The Outline nests by what actually contains what. An object expression inside an init block was filed under whichever property came last, and the breadcrumb read Holder then disposable then the object.

One chevron per line. A property declared in a primary constructor sits on its class's own line and produced a second fold that stopped partway through the class, so folding the class folded a fragment. 181 lines carried two.
A parameter no longer swallows the documentation of the one after it.
